$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. ExecutionRequest per FB-RAT-EXE-001. Typically carried as the `payload` of a ContractEnvelope<ExecutionRequest> (see schemas/common/envelope.schema.json). `id` is this object's own FB-RAT-COM-002 stable ID, distinct from the envelope's objectId.
title: ExecutionRequest
description: A request to run a typed operation against a specific ExecutionTarget (by id — not embedded, see schemas/execution/target.schema.json). Structurally operationalizes: FB-RAT-EXE-007 (secret handles, never raw values), FB-RAT-EXE-008 (external idempotency key + duplicate behavior declared before execution), FB-RAT-COM-012 (no contract bypass — `authorityGrant` is required, never optional, so a request cannot skip the authority seam), and the platform-grounding MUST-rule that an open-ended operation class MUST NOT declare fgsType DATA_SYNC or MEDIA_PROCESSING (Service.onTimeout() would kill it mid-work with no extension).

id.description: Globally unique stable ID for this request (FB-RAT-COM-002).

targetId.description: References an ExecutionTarget.id (schemas/execution/target.schema.json). Not embedded — a request outlives the exact target snapshot it was issued against; ExecutionReceipt.targetSnapshot is where a point-in-time copy lives.

operationClass.description: Coarse operation shape. This field is descriptive/routing only — it is NOT what the MUST-level fgsType rule below keys off of (that is `openEnded`, declared explicitly by the caller) — because whether a given BUILD or CUSTOM operation is open-ended is provider- and workload-specific, not implied by class alone.

command.description: The command/entrypoint to run, in whatever form the target's provider expects (a shell command line for SSH_HOST/RASPBERRY_PI/LOCAL_ANDROID; a workflow file ref for GITHUB_ACTIONS/GITEA_ACTIONS).

args.description: Positional/flag arguments, kept separate from `command` so a provider can shell-escape them correctly rather than string-concatenating.

workingDirectory.description: Working directory on the target, or null to use the provider's default (e.g. the checked-out repo root).

workingRevision.description: Git commit SHA, branch, or tag the operation runs against (FB-RAT-STR-004 revision visibility). Null only for operations with no git-scoped working tree (e.g. a bare device-flash or a connectivity probe).

envVars.description: Non-secret environment variables only. FB-RAT-EXE-007 and the binding API-key rule (CLAUDE.md rule 5, 'never logged, never sent anywhere except the provider they belong to') require any secret-bearing value to be referenced through `secretHandles` instead — this map has no field capable of carrying a raw secret value by design, only named non-secret key/value pairs. A producer populating this map with a credential-shaped value is a binding-rule violation the schema cannot catch structurally (JSON Schema has no way to know a string is a live API key) — see fixtures/execution/adversarial/request-secret-value-in-envvars.adversarial.json.

handleId.description: Opaque reference into the Android-Keystore-backed secret store (security/KeystoreSecret.kt) — never the secret value itself (FB-RAT-EXE-007).

purpose.description: What this secret is for, e.g. 'github.pat', 'anthropic.api_key' — purpose-bound, so a provider cannot silently repurpose a handle issued for one destination to authenticate to a different one.

secretHandles.description: FB-RAT-EXE-007: purpose-bound secret handles this request needs resolved at execution time. This array structurally cannot carry a secret VALUE — there is no `value`/`secret`/`token` field in the handle shape, only `handleId` + `purpose` — by construction, not by convention alone.

wallClockSeconds.description: Wall-clock budget for the whole operation, or null for provider-default. A provider MUST refuse to start an `openEnded: true` request that also has `wallClockSeconds: null` AND `fgsType` in {DATA_SYNC, MEDIA_PROCESSING} — structurally impossible here since that fgsType/openEnded combination is already rejected by the top-level if/then below regardless of wallClockSeconds; this field exists for the remaining cases (SPECIAL_USE, CONNECTED_DEVICE, NONE) where a bound is still good practice but not structurally forced.

maxOutputBytes.description: Cap on captured stdout/stderr/log bytes, or null for provider-default.

maxSessionSeconds.description: Bounded session length after which the provider MUST require a fresh explicit user re-authorization before continuing (platform-grounding requirement — open-ended agent loops/terminals do not get an indefinite grant just because the operation itself has no natural end).

requiresUserReauth.description: Whether reaching maxSessionSeconds requires an explicit user action to continue (true) or the provider is allowed to auto-renew within the same authorityGrant scope (false — only valid when the authorityGrant itself was issued with an explicit multi-session allowance).

thermalStateObservabilityRequired.description: FB-RAT-EXE-006, P0-normative half: the provider MUST be able to report thermal state for the duration of this request. This is the normative half of EXE-006. Defaults to true; a provider incapable of thermal observability MUST NOT accept a request with this field true (schema cannot enforce that acceptance-time refusal itself — see docs/ratified/EXECUTION_CONTRACT.md §5).

thermalPausePolicyRef.description: EXPERIMENTAL, not ratified — FB-RAT-EXE-006's pause/offload POLICY half. Optional pointer into docs/non_ratified/EXPERIMENTAL_DECISIONS.md's thermal-policy entry (owned by a separate agent/session). Null means no thermal pause/offload policy is in effect for this request; that is the only ratified default. A non-null value here MUST NOT be treated as binding — only as an experimental hint.

grantId.description: Reference to a grant issued by the Execution Contract + Authority engine (WP-0 survey (c) — a separate, create-new domain not detailed by this file's object model). This is the minimal reference shape the execution domain needs to refuse to model requests outside the authority seam (FB-RAT-COM-012 'no contract bypass' — anything that skips authority is a prototype, not architecture); the full grant/capability-ladder shape belongs to that other domain and is not invented here.

scopes.description: Operation scopes this grant authorizes, matching vocabulary from the target's CapabilityManifest.supportedOperations where applicable.

authorityGrant.description: Required and non-null on every ExecutionRequest (FB-RAT-COM-012) — there is no shape of this contract that omits an authority grant reference.

role.description: What this expected output is for, e.g. 'build-artifact', 'log-bundle', 'flash-verify-report'.

expectedOutputs.description: Lightweight descriptors of outputs this request expects to produce — not full ArtifactRef entries (schemas/common/artifact-ref.schema.json), because the actual artifacts do not exist yet at request time. ExecutionReceipt.outputs is where realized ArtifactRefs (reused from common, not redefined) appear.

idempotencyKey.description: FB-RAT-COM-006 / FB-RAT-EXE-008: caller-supplied de-duplication key. Required non-null (see the if/then below) whenever `sideEffectExternal` is true — an external side effect (CI dispatch, device flash, git push) MUST declare its idempotency key and duplicate behavior BEFORE execution, not after the fact.

sideEffectExternal.description: True when this operation causes a side effect outside the immediate execution process/session — e.g. dispatching a CI workflow, flashing a device, pushing to a git host. Drives the FB-RAT-EXE-008 if/then below.

externalDuplicateBehavior.description: FB-RAT-EXE-008: what a provider MUST do when it observes a retried request carrying an idempotencyKey it has already seen. Required non-null whenever `sideEffectExternal` is true.

openEnded.description: True for work with no natural bounded end declared up front — agent loops, interactive terminal sessions, long-running builds without a caller-supplied wallClockSeconds. Drives the platform-grounding MUST-rule below: an `openEnded: true` request MUST NOT declare `fgsType` DATA_SYNC or MEDIA_PROCESSING, because both carry a hard 6h/rolling-24h ceiling with no extension (Service.onTimeout()) that open-ended work cannot honor safely.

specialUseJustification.description: Required non-null (and non-empty) when `fgsType` is SPECIAL_USE — the manifest justification string Play review requires for a specialUse foreground service. Null for every other fgsType.

unknownFields.description: Bag for fields a decoder received but did not recognize, preserved for round-trip (FB-RAT-COM-003).

allOf.$comment: Structural enforcement of the platform-grounding MUST-rule: an operation class targeting open-ended work MUST NOT declare fgsType DATA_SYNC or MEDIA_PROCESSING. See fixtures/execution/invalid/request-open-ended-datasync-rejected.invalid.json.
FB-RAT-EXE-008: external ops MUST declare idempotency key + duplicate behavior before execution.
SPECIAL_USE FGS requires a manifest justification string (platform grounding).

FgsType.description: Duplicated from schemas/execution/target.schema.json's $defs/FgsType per this repo's established convention of duplicating small shared sub-shapes across schema files rather than reaching into another document's $defs (see docs/ratified/COMMON_CONVENTIONS.md §5) — both copies MUST be kept in sync if this vocabulary changes.
